boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten named Stanford destinations for a no-purchase outing. Walk, bike, or use transit to avoid visitor-parking charges where applicable.

cards.title: Browse the Cantor galleries
cards.subtitle: 328 Lomita Drive, Stanford
cards.notes: Meet at the museum entrance, choose a gallery or exhibition together, then compare one work each before heading back across campus.
cards.short_summary: A free public art-museum visit with galleries, exhibitions, and outdoor sculpture nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford states that Cantor Arts Center admission, tours, public programs, and family activities are always free and that the museum is open to the public.
cards.source_title: About the Cantor | Cantor Arts Center
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; check the museum's current hours before going. Visitor parking may cost extra.

cards.title: Look through modern art together
cards.subtitle: 314 Lomita Drive, Stanford
cards.notes: Pick a few galleries to see at an unhurried pace, then use the lobby or nearby outdoor space to trade reactions to the artworks.
cards.short_summary: A free museum of modern and contemporary American art beside the Cantor.
cards.evidence_claim: The Anderson Collection’s visitor page describes it as a free museum of modern and contemporary American art.
cards.source_title: Visit | Anderson Collection at Stanford University
cards.access_notes: Open Thursday through Monday, 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; visitor parking payments are separate.

cards.title: Walk the Dish trail
cards.subtitle: Stanford Dish conservation area, Stanford
cards.notes: Bring water, start a conversation-friendly loop, and pause at viewpoints rather than treating the route as a race or a workout challenge.
cards.short_summary: A year-round hiking and jogging destination in Stanford’s foothills.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford describes the Dish as open year-round for hiking and jogging and identifies five miles of trails in the conservation area.
cards.access_notes: Open year-round; follow Dish-area rules, including the no-pets policy. Stanford says much of its arts and athletics offerings are free and public.

cards.title: Take a cactus-garden loop
cards.subtitle: Arizona Garden, south of the Mausoleum, Stanford
cards.notes: Stroll the planted paths, photograph forms and textures without touching plants, and pair the stop with the nearby mausoleum area.
cards.short_summary: A historic garden of cacti and succulents designed for the Stanford family.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford identifies the Arizona Garden as a historic garden with cacti and succulents, located off Quarry Road between Campus Drive and Arboretum Road.
cards.source_title: Arizona Garden | Stanford LBRE Facilities Operations
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus destination; visit on foot or bike to avoid potential visitor-parking charges. Stanford says much of campus arts is free and open to the public.

cards.entity_name: Stanford Family Mausoleum and Angel of Grief
cards.title: Visit the mausoleum area
cards.subtitle: Stanford Arboretum, Stanford
cards.notes: Walk the area quietly, look at the mausoleum, family statue, and Angel of Grief, and keep the visit respectful of its memorial setting.
cards.short_summary: A historic Stanford Arboretum destination with memorial sculpture and family history.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford Visitor Information directs visitors to the mausoleum area to see the Stanford Family Mausoleum, Stanford Family statue, and Angel of Grief.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus destination; use respectful conduct. Stanford says much of its campus arts is free and open to the public.

cards.title: Walk around Lake Lagunita
cards.subtitle: Lake Lagunita, Stanford
cards.notes: Meet for a low-key walk or sit nearby to talk; stay on permitted paths and give wildlife and restoration areas plenty of space.
cards.short_summary: A campus lake area Stanford specifically suggests for walking, running, or enjoying the view.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford Visitor Information describes Lake Lagunita as a place to run, walk, or enjoy the view.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus destination; conditions can vary because the lake may be dry. Stanford says much of its campus arts is free and open to the public.

cards.title: Spread out on the Oval
cards.subtitle: The Oval and Palm Drive, Stanford
cards.notes: Bring a blanket if you have one, sit beneath the trees, play a casual game, or simply take a break while watching campus activity.
cards.short_summary: A campus gateway and open lawn Stanford identifies for picnics, volleyball, and relaxing.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford Visitor Information says the Oval is a relaxing spot for students, faculty, and community members to have picnics, play volleyball, and enjoy the weather.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor open space; bring your own activity items if desired. Stanford says much of its campus arts is free and open to the public.

cards.title: Find the Papua New Guinea carvings
cards.subtitle: Papua New Guinea Sculpture Garden, Stanford
cards.notes: Walk through the garden slowly, identify different figures and materials, and use the visitor page’s context to guide a shared discussion.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor garden with 40 wood and stone carvings made by visiting Sepik River artists.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford Visitor Information states that the garden contains 40 wood and stone carvings created on-site in 1994 by ten artists from Papua New Guinea’s inland Sepik River area.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus artwork; view respectfully and do not climb or touch sculptures. Stanford says much of its campus arts is free and open to the public.

cards.title: Walk Memorial Court and the Quad
cards.subtitle: Memorial Court, Main Quad entrance, Stanford
cards.notes: Use the arcades as a meeting point, look for the Rodin sculptures, and continue through the Main Quad at a relaxed pace.
cards.short_summary: The Main Quad entrance with multiple Auguste Rodin sculptures and campus architecture.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford Visitor Information identifies Memorial Court as the main entrance to the Main Quad from Palm Drive and notes that it features several sculptures by Auguste Rodin.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus destination; access may be affected by university events. Stanford says much of its campus arts is free and open to the public.

cards.title: Meet by Terman Fountain
cards.subtitle: Terman Fountain, Stanford
cards.notes: Use the fountain as a simple outdoor rendezvous point, take a short break in the surrounding space, and continue your campus walk together.
cards.short_summary: A named campus fountain Stanford highlights as a place for students to relax.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford Visitor Information identifies Terman Fountain as a campus destination and says it is a location where students wade and relax while on campus.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus destination; do not assume wading is permitted—follow posted rules. Stanford says much of its campus arts is free and open to the public.

warnings: Free status refers to admission or participation at the destination; transportation, food, equipment, and visitor parking can cost extra.
